name: evtx_carve
description: Recover event records from a blob that is not an event log: sweeps for ElfChnk chunk headers in unallocated space, a pagefile, a memory image or a truncated .evtx, checks that the 128 bytes after each ElfChnk signature are a chunk header (header size 0x80, the record offsets inside the 64 KiB, the first record number not past the last: python-evtx's ChunkHeader accepts garbage, so the tool checks), verifies each real chunk's own checksums and parses the records inside it. A signature that fails the header check is a problem line (a page, the whole list in a file) and counts only under candidates and signatures_rejected, never as a chunk found or parsed. Every matching record is kept with its whole XML in a file the answer names (written whenever anything was found); the inline records are the summary, without the XML unless with_xml is true. A repeated EventData name is kept as a list, not overwritten. chunk_limit (chunks parsed) and candidate_limit (places where the magic was found, built into a chunk or not) bound the work of one call, not the result: the sweep stops before the next one and resume_start is the offset to pass as start. The answer says the range asked for and the range examined, and sweep_complete means that range was swept, not that every record that ever existed was recovered. Problems are a page with the whole list in a file. A chunk whose checksums do not verify may still hold sound records, and is marked chunk_verified false. A chunk whose header passes but whose checksums do not hold and from which no record can be read is a problem line (probably not a chunk), not a clean find. A chunk whose string or template table loops or points outside the chunk is not given to python-evtx (which follows them without end): it is a problem line and counted under chunks_not_read_tables, and what the library does with any other chunk runs under a timer of 8 seconds, after which the chunk is given up and named. A record whose XML is not well-formed (python-evtx does not escape a quote in an attribute) is kept in the result file with parse_error and its XML, and counted under records_malformed_kept. The sweep stops at its own time limit (590 seconds) with resume_start; SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP finish the result file and end it with the answer (status interrupted, exit 128 plus the signal, resume_start the chunk being read when it stopped, whose records may already be in the file). channels shows at most 100 channels (channel_count, and every channel in the file all_channels names). Result file names are made from the path, the range, the event ids, whether contains was given, chunk_limit and candidate_limit, never from the needle, and no result file is ever replaced: the same result is named again, another takes the next free -n name. Records after a chunk's free-space offset (the slack of a recycled chunk) are not read. Every answer and refusal carries status and status_basis. A carved record belongs to the channel it names, not to the file it was found in. SENSITIVE: carved records hold command lines, script text and arguments that can include a secret, and a pagefile or memory image can hold records of any process; run it as a job with secret_output: true when they may. WITHHOLDING (one boundary on every way out). Every key and value of the answer, and every row of every file this tool writes, is judged by the type of the field it fills (channel, computer, provider, EventData names and values, and the XML): a name, path, key or URL is shown as it is only when it fits a plain grammar (a path component by component; GUIDs, SIDs, addresses, 0x numbers, times and hexadecimal ids up to 24 digits are plain), free text has token-shaped runs, user-info, the value after a secret's name, vendor-prefixed tokens, padded base64 and PEM keys withheld, and a second check written apart from the first reads it all once more (a string it replaces makes a complete answer partial and is listed under boundary.replaced_at). A withheld text is <withheld N characters: reason>. Binary data written as hexadecimal is decoded and judged by its printable text. A filter on content (contains) is applied to the text that is shown, never to what is withheld. write_values: true writes the originals of everything withheld to <tool>-values.jsonl (mode 0600, created first, never replaced) and is accepted only in a job the harness runs as secret output (the manifest declares it; SECRET_OUTPUT=1), refused as JSON anywhere else before anything is made. EventData fields are typed by name (SID, GUID, hash, address, time, path and registry key fields); every other field is free text. Measured on 1,000 random plants per shape and context (175 cells): prefixed tokens (GitHub, GitLab, Stripe, SendGrid, Google, npm, AWS key ids), JWT, PEM keys, connection strings, user-info (also with an @ inside the password), NUL, zero-width and full-width splits, case-folded and glued prefixes: none printed whole; AWS-shaped, 16, 20 and 32-byte base64 keys: at most 2.2% (letters-only keys with a slash); random base62 of 20 to 40 characters: at most 0.5%; random lower-case letters of 24: 9.4%; a 16-character base32 seed: 11%. Real Windows strings changed (any part withheld) in 9,950 generated registry, file, service, package and host names, SIDs, GUIDs and typed digests (2 changed: the 32-digit hash in a Chrome and an Edge autolaunch value name) and 3,431 strings of real event logs (25 changed: 17 of 1,040 whole event records, 7 of 313 command lines and messages, 1 of 322 path fields; they hold encoded PowerShell payloads and the 32-digit hash directories of the .NET native-image cache). NOT recognised, by design: a secret that does not look like one (a plain password or passphrase, a pronounceable passphrase, a UUID-shaped key, a hexadecimal secret of up to 24 digits, anything under 16 characters in a name; 75% to 100% of such plants are printed): withholding is by shape, so a file whose secrets matter is read in a job run with secret_output: true.

path.description: A raw blob: unallocated output, pagefile.sys, a memory image, or a damaged .evtx

contains.description: Keep only records whose XML contains this string, case-insensitive

start.description: Byte offset to start the sweep at (default 0)

max_bytes.description: Stop the sweep after this many bytes from start (at least 1)

chunk_limit.description: Chunks to parse in one call (default 200). When more remain the sweep stops before the next chunk and resume_start names the offset to pass as start; nothing before it is skipped

limit.description: Records shown inline (default 300, an inline page size); every matching record, with its XML, is in the file named by all_results

with_xml.description: Include each record's full XML in the inline records too (the file always has it)

candidate_limit.description: Chunk-magic hits to examine in one call (default 20000), whether or not each builds into a chunk; the sweep stops before the next and resume_start names where to carry on

write_values.description: Write the originals of everything the boundary withheld to a file under $OUT (mode 0600, created first, never replaced): only in a job run with secret_output: true, refused anywhere else; default false
